{{Quote|For superior balance, use the Niman form. This form has no specific strengths, but no weaknesses either.|[[Kavar]]|<ref name="TSL" />}}
'''Form VI''', also known as '''Niman''', '''the Way of the Rancor''', '''the Moderation Form''', and '''the diplomat's form''', was the sixth form of the seven forms of [[Lightsaber combat/Legends|lightsaber combat]]. This fighting style was a hybrid martial art created by effectively combining elements of the preceding [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]] forms into a single, generalized form. Niman balanced out between the various specializations of the other forms, covering many of the basic moves, but focusing on overall moderation. This resulted in a fighting style that lacked a significant advantage, but also lacking any serious drawbacks, and thereby not leaving adherents as exposed as some of the more aggressive or specialized forms. Overall, Niman had a fairly relaxed focus on bladework, designed as a simple, easily learned fighting form for [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] who preferred to devote most of their time to study and diplomacy. although, if it was mastered (a difficult process), it could be absolutely deadly in the hands of a skilled practitioner, as demonstrated by such individuals as [[Exar Kun/Legends|Exar Kun]].

To compensate for the relaxed focus on bladework and lack of significant specialization, Niman training regimens encouraged the inclusion of [[The Force/Legends|Force]]-based attacks in combat, such as [[Telekinesis/Legends|telekinetic]] pulls and shoves used in sync with lightsaber strikes. As Niman was developed from two pre-existing martial arts fighting forms that both emphasized the use of dual-blades, it provided a firm foundation for duelists looking to study into such practices. Ultimately, Niman's success in combat was dependent on a specific practitioner's intuition and creativity in combat, rather than the rote responses common to the other forms.

==History==
[[File:SimpleSolution-TSS.jpg|thumb|left|250px|[[Rachi Sitra]], a [[Jedi archaeologist]], was an adherent of the moderation form.]]

The original Niman fighting style was practiced by the [[Royale Machetero]]s of the [[Kashi Mer Dynasty]], who named it for the dual triumvirate of the [[Niman|Kashi deities]]. The style was adopted by the [[Legions of Lettow]], a group of [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|Dark-siders]] involved in the [[First Great Schism]] of the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]]. After the defeat of the Legion at the hands of the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]], Niman was adopted by the Jedi Order, eventually being refined into the sixth form of [[Lightsaber combat/Legends|lightsaber combat]], referred to by the same name.<ref name="TCSWE">''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''</ref> While Form VI was largely adapted from this earlier fighting style, several noted Jedi considered the pure root of Form VI to be [[Form III/Legends|Form III]]. Being a "jack-of-all-trades" style with broad emphasis and little need for continuous and dedicated practice, Niman found a niche amongst [[Jedi Consular]]s who instead preferred to focus on diplomacy and meditation on [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] rather than combat.<ref name="TJP">[[The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force (real-life book)|''The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force'']]</ref> Ironically, Niman became the chosen discipline of the fallen Jedi-turned-[[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]], [[Exar Kun/Legends|Exar Kun]].<ref name="KotOR CG">''[[Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide]]''</ref>

During the various wars against the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]], Niman was prized by some for its general versatility on the battlefield, though heavily criticized by others for being insufficiently demanding.<ref name="RoT">''[[Darth Bane: Rule of Two]]''</ref> Over time, it became the standard in [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]] training, and by the start of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], was one of the most common forms in the Jedi Order.<ref name="JvS:EGTF">[[Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force (real-life book)|''Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force'']]</ref> However, Niman demonstrated itself to be inadequate for the open battlefields of the Clone Wars, proven when all the Form VI adherents involved in the [[First Battle of Geonosis/Legends|First Battle of Geonosis]] died in combat.<ref name="SW.com Fightsaber">{{SWArchive|url=games/videogames/news20080728.html|text=Fightsaber: Mastering the Art of Lightsaber Combat}}</ref> In the post-war years, Niman remained studied and practiced amongst the Sith while the Jedi were hunted down in the [[Great Jedi Purge/Legends|Great Jedi Purge]].<ref name="TFU2novel">[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II (novelization)|''The Force Unleashed'' novel]]</ref> Form VI lightsaber combat would eventually be rediscovered by the [[New Jedi Order]], though until then, it was effectively replaced as the favored "jack-of-all-trades" fighting style by the [[Medium style]] of lightsaber combat.<ref name="JediKnight">''[[Star Wars: Jedi Knight: Dark Forces II]]''</ref>

==Description==
{{Quote|It is often referred to as the diplomat's form because it is less intensive in its demands than other disciplines, allowing Jedi to spend more time developing their skills in perception, political strategy, and negotiation.|[[Cin Drallig/Legends|Cin Drallig]]|<ref name="JvS:EGTF" />}}
[[File:Form6Niman-SWGTCG.jpg|thumb|right|200px|A Jedi in the Niman low-guard stance.]]
A hybrid fighting style, Niman incorporated elements from the previous forms, mainly [[Form I/Legends|Forms I]] through [[Form V/Legends|V]], excluding [[Form II/Legends|Form II]],<ref name="SW.com Fightsaber" /> but balanced out between their various specializations, in keeping with the Jedi quest to achieve harmony and justice without resorting to the rule of power. Form VI covered many of the various moves of lightsaber combat, but due to its emphasis on overall moderation, its focus on bladework was somewhat relaxed. Thusly, the form was easily mastered by those who preferred to devote a high percentage of their time to study and peacekeeping, which made it the preferred form of Jedi Consulars. While the generalization made it ill-suited for lightsaber dueling or fighting on the open battlefield, it was perfectly adequate for facing down criminals and thugs.<ref name="Fightsaber: Jedi Lightsaber Combat" /><ref name="TJP" /> Due to its "jack-of-all-trades" nature, the success of this form was largely dependent on the practitioner's intuition, improvisation, and creativity in combat rather than the rote responses derived from other forms.

To compensate for this relaxed focus on bladework, Niman training regimens encouraged adherents of the style to incorporate [[Force power/Legends|Force powers]] into combat. Proper management of these tools allowed a Form VI master to control and eliminate an entire group of enemies, though many lower level initiates experienced difficulty attempting this.<ref name="TJP" /> As Form VI lightsaber combat was derived from the dual-bladed Niman style practiced by the Royale Macheteros of the Kashi Mer, it provided a foundation for the challenging practice.<ref name="TCSWE" /> However, while hailed as a practical, all-around fighting form, it was heavily criticized by many for being insufficiently demanding. It should be noted that while Niman provided no decisive edge in battle, it achieved its worth by not leaving its wielder as exposed as some of the more aggressive forms.<ref name="Fightsaber: Jedi Lightsaber Combat" /> Due to the relaxed bladework of the form, it was said that most Niman practitioners would find it almost impossible to defeat a Makashi practitioner.<ref name="TJP" />

According to [[Battlemaster/Legends|Jedi Battlemaster]] [[Cin Drallig/Legends|Cin Drallig]], if a duelist dedicated himself exclusively to Form VI, he could expect to study the style for at least ten years before achieving mastery.<ref name="JvS:EGTF" />

===Moves and Maneuvers===
{{Quote|To compensate for the relaxed focus on bladework, Form VI encourages integrating Force powers into combat.|[[Skarch Vaunk]], [[Battlemaster/Legends|Jedi Battlemaster]], in ''[[The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force]]''|<ref name="TJP" />}}
[[File:NimanPushingSlash2.jpg|thumb|left|250px|The ''pushing slash'' technique.]]

The opening stance of the Niman form was wide and open, with the blade held out from the body in a one-handed grip, the blade angled upwards and back, while the off-hand was folded across the chest. The feet were evenly spaced.<ref name="MysteriesOfTheJedi">''[[Star Wars: Mysteries of the Jedi]]''</ref> Another Niman stance featured the blade held at head-height in a two-handed grip, angled upwards and slightly in, with the dominant foot placed forwards.<ref name="RotS VD">''[[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref> A third position was a two-handed low guard, with the hilt held at waist height in both hands, blade held back and to the side, angled downwards, with the feet closely spaced.<ref name="SoCNimanCard">{{SWGTCG|set=Squadrons Over Corellia|cardname=Niman}}</ref>

In keeping with the tactic of incorporating Force powers into combat, two primary Form VI maneuvers, the "draw closer" and the "pushing slash", were conjunctions between lightsaber moves and [[Telekinesis/Legends|telekinetic attacks]]. Effectively polar opposites of one another, the "draw closer" involved telekinetically seizing an opponent and pulling the enemy into the path of his blade, while the "pushing slash" slammed the opponent with a Force push after scoring an attack.<ref name="JATM">''[[Jedi Academy Training Manual]]''</ref><ref name="TJP" />

===Applications===
{{Quote|Is Form VI the most worthy of study? No, but in general it is the most practical.|[[Cin Drallig/Legends|Cin Drallig]]|<ref name="JvS:EGTF" />}}
Derived from a fighting form centered around the use of dual-blades, Niman was considered a foundation for this challenging practice, and became something of a gateway form to [[Jar'Kai/Legends|Jar'Kai]]. Form VI dual-blade training encouraged the use of the [[Shoto lightsaber/Legends|shoto short lightsaber]] in the off-hand, as the smaller blade was easier to handle. A notable Jar'Kai master was the [[Priapulin]] [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Skwelli]], who carried six lightsabers. He was renowned for his skill in his era, and recordings of his fighting form were considered a wonder to behold. Many modern Jedi mirrored this attitude, though [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]] was a notable exception, who, in his copy of [[The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force|''The Jedi Path'']], labeled Skwelli's form and footwork as sloppy. [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] simply commented on his hope that he never had to face a [[Grievous/Legends|duelist with such an array of weapons]].<ref name="TJP" /> Niman was commonly studied by duelists looking to brush up on dual-blade combat, though few actually mastered Niman itself, as this required at least ten years of study.<ref name="TCSWE" />

[[File:Exarkunversusbaas.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Exar Kun wielding dual-blades during a sparring match with Vodo-Siosk Baas.]]
Exar Kun chose to specialize in Niman, and while there was little doubt that he found the dual-blade training regiments useful when he converted [[Exar Kun's lightsaber/Legends|his lightsaber]] into a [[Double-bladed lightsaber/Legends|double-bladed weapon]], he often preferred to fight with a single blade. His skill marked him as one of the finest duelists of his era, demonstrated when he defeated his instructor, renowned [[Jedi Weapon Master]] [[Vodo-Siosk Baas]], in a sparring match, indicating his mastery of the fighting form. However, rather than adhere to its philosophy of moderation over aggression, Kun was a vicious duelist who favored brutal power moves and had little compunction against lashing out against his foes with physical attacks. These tendencies were exacerbated by his turn to the dark side of the Force, when he actively took to drawing on his rage in combat. However, while he failed to observe the core concepts of Form VI, Kun was never defeated in a lightsaber duel, and only his fellow Darksider, [[Ulic Qel-Droma/Legends|Ulic Qel-Droma]], was able to match him on neutral ground. It should be noted however that, aside from sparring matches, Kun was only known to have participated in three lightsaber duels over the course of his career.<ref name="KotOR CG" /><ref name="TotJdlots">''[[Star Wars: Tales of the Jedi – Dark Lords of the Sith]]''</ref><ref name="TotJtsw">''[[Star Wars: Tales of the Jedi – The Sith War]]''</ref>

Many Niman maneuvers incorporated the use of Force powers chained into the combat sequences, to compensate for the relaxed focus on bladework. While he favored Form V lightsaber combat, [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] had studied Niman and occasionally favored such practices.<ref name="TJP" /><ref name="JediCrash">{{TCW|Jedi Crash}}</ref> His master, Obi-Wan Kenobi, also occasionally applied such skills, having studied Niman to learn this tactic. Kenobi commented in his copy of ''The Jedi Path'' that he found this practice extremely difficult, indicating his need for more practice.<ref name="TJP" /> During the [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|Invasion of Naboo]], Kenobi had evidently developed an advanced level of skill in this application, frequently blasting aside [[Battle droid/Legends|battle droids]] with Force pushes while in combat.<ref name="TPM">{{Film|I}}</ref>

==Practitioners==
{{Quote|The Jedi Council maintains that Form VI best suits the role of contemporary Jedi Knights. After all, a Jedi Knight who is overly trained in martial combat might be at a loss to resolve a complex political conflict or a sensitive trade disagreement.|[[Cin Drallig/Legends|Cin Drallig]]|<ref name="JvS:EGTF" />}}
[[File:LostJedi-KOTOR2.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Kavar, Vrook Lamar, and Zez-Kai Ell, all Form VI instructors.]]
Ironically for a fighting form designed to encourage moderation over aggression, Niman was the chosen discipline of the fallen Jedi-turned-Sith Lord Exar Kun. Trained by famed Jedi Weapon Master Vodo-Siosk Baas, Kun was one of the finest duelists of the age, even defeating his own master in a sparring match.<ref name="KotOR CG" /><ref name="TotJdlots" /> Adhering more closely to the philosophy of Form VI were [[Zez-Kai Ell]], [[Vrook Lamar]], and [[Kavar]], Jedi Council Masters active during the [[Jedi Civil War]] and [[First Jedi Purge]] who had mastered Niman sufficiently to act as instructors in the style. They typically taught the form to [[Jedi Sentinel/Legends|Jedi Sentinels]].<ref name="TSL" />

During the [[New Sith Wars]], Niman was practiced amongst both the Jedi and the Sith forces. A notable Jedi adherent was [[Johun Othone]], who took full advantage of Form VI's inherent versatility during the pitched battles of the war. However, during the post-war years, he made little effort to maintain his skills as a swordsman, instead focusing on his diplomatic talents, and his skills atrophied considerably.<ref name="RoT" /> The [[Sith Blademaster]], [[Kas'im]], included full mastery of Niman in his repertoire of skills, and trained many [[Sith apprentice/Legends|Sith apprentices]] in the style. It should be noted that while Kas'im was versed in dual-blade combat, using it to great effect against [[Darth Bane/Legends|Darth Bane]] during their [[Duel on Lehon|duel to the death]], Kas'im instead relied on [[Form IV/Legends|Form IV]] dual-blade training rather than Niman.<ref name="PoD" />

[[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]] may have mastered Niman just as he had mastered all the other six forms of lightsaber combat. In addition to being extremely well-versed in Niman's dual-bladed variant, he was also outstandingly adept in incorporating force attacks in his lightsaber style. His knowledge was competent enough to adequately teach his student, [[Darth Maul/Legends|Darth Maul]], the art of Niman, causing the latter to become decently capable at it, especially in its function of incorporating Force attacks into his dueling style.<ref name="TotG">''[[Threats of the Galaxy]]''</ref> Obi-Wan Kenobi studied Niman during his apprenticeship under [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]], attempting to learn how to apply the Force while in the midst of combat, a practice he commented as being difficult but eventually mastered enough to seamlessly Force Push droids. Kenobi's own student, Anakin Skywalker, studied Form VI to develop his skills with dual-blades, though he commented that he was working on this mostly as an exercise in control, and was doubtful that he would ever need to apply it.<ref name="TJP" /> Skywalker's assumption was proven wrong when he wielded dual lightsabers against Dooku during the First Battle of Geonosis, and several other times during the Clone Wars.<ref name="AOTCm">{{Film|II}}</ref> Anakin frequently used his Niman training to incorporate use of the Force into his dueling style and also had advanced his abilities in the form enough to instruct his Padawan Ahsoka Tano in the lower levels of the style as a training exercise. As Darth Vader, he started incorporating elements of Niman swordplay alongside the other forms after retooling his dueling style and retained his advanced skill in Niman's techniques of incorporating the use of the Force in combat. Dooku also possessed considerable skill in Niman from his time as a Lightsaber Instructor of the Jedi Temple, enough so to instruct the [[Kaleesh/Legends|Kaleesh]] cyborg Grievous in it, as well as to coach Grievous while he passed his training on to his [[IG-100 MagnaGuard/Legends|IG-100 MagnaGuard]] bodyguards.<ref name="LoE">''[[Labyrinth of Evil]]''</ref> Dooku applied his mastery of Niman to masterfully use the Force in conjunction with lightsaber combat.

While Form VI was not a weak fighting style per say, it was an inadequate form for the open battlefields of the Clone Wars. Notably, all adherents of the style involved in the Battle of [[Geonosis/Legends|Geonosis]] perished, prominent practitioners including [[Sarrissa Jeng/Legends|Sarrissa Jeng]], [[Sar Labooda/Legends|Sar Labooda]], and [[Joclad Danva/Legends|Joclad Danva]].<ref name="SW.com Fightsaber" /> Danva's death was an especially sore loss for the Jedi Order, as he was among their most renowned duelists and martial artists, and master of Jar'Kai dual-blade fencing, one of the styles that Form VI lightsaber combat was derived from.<ref name="MS1:BattleSurgeons">''[[MedStar I: Battle Surgeons]]''</ref> However, Form VI adherents and trainees nonetheless remained, with Anakin Skywalker instructing his [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]], [[Ahsoka Tano/Legends|Ahsoka Tano]], in the lower levels of the style as a training exercise.<ref name="Wild Space">''[[The Clone Wars: Wild Space]]''</ref> Tano would later take to wielding a shoto in her off-hand, in keeping with Niman dual-blade training.<ref name="CWS3">[[The Clone Wars: Season Three|''The Clone Wars'': Season Three]]</ref> Grandmaster [[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]] and Swordmaster [[Mace Windu/Legends|Mace Windu]] were also proficient in Niman, as they were said to have fully mastered all forms of lightsaber combat, although only Windu ever displayed proficiency in the form's function of incorporating Force Attacks into his lightsaber combat. [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] Cin Drallig was considered the most prolific instructor of Form VI, as he was of the five forms below it, teaching Niman to thousands of students during his Jedi career.<ref name="Order 66">{{InsiderCite|87|Order 66: Destroy All Jedi}}</ref> However, despite his skills and mastery, Drallig was ultimately cut down by the Form V specialist Darth Vader during [[Operation: Knightfall/Legends|Operation Knightfall]], part of the [[Great Jedi Purge/Legends|Great Jedi Purge]], although he put up a fierce fight.<ref name="ROTSf">{{Film|III}}</ref>

Students of Niman active during the Purge include [[Rachi Sitra]],<ref name="Moderation">''{{SWGTCG|set=Galactic Hunters|cardname=Moderation}}''</ref> and Vader's apprentice, [[Galen Marek]]. However, Marek chose to devote himself to Forms III and V rather than VI, though he still incorporated powerful telekinetic attacks into his lightsaber sequences, a common element in Form VI training. His clone, [[Subject 1138|Starkiller]], made much more avid use of Niman, actively specializing in the style to develop his skills with dual-blades. Starkiller's knowledge of the form was based off of inherited memory flashes from his genetic template.<ref name="StarkillerNote">[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II (novelization)|''Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II'' novelization]]: Starkiller's knowledge of Niman is specified as having been inherited from Galen Marek, establishing that the latter has at least received instruction in Form VI</ref> Despite the limited battlefield benefits provided by Form VI, it remained in use up until and beyond the resurgence and takeover of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], a notable practitioner being the Dark Lord of the Sith, [[Darth Krayt]].<ref name="LECG">''[[Legacy Era Campaign Guide]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
Niman was first described in the ''[[Fightsaber: Jedi Lightsaber Combat]]'' article in [[Star Wars Insider 62|''Star Wars Insider'' 62]], written by [[David West Reynolds]] and fencer Jack "Stelen" Bobo, identified it as Form VI lightsaber combat. The proper name of the form, "Niman", as well as its alternate titles as the "Moderation Form" and the "Way of the [[Rancor/Legends|Rancor]]" would be specified in later sources.<ref name="SW:Lightsabers">''[[Star Wars: Lightsabers: A Guide to Weapons of the Force]]''</ref><ref name="TJP" /> Notably, the ''Fightsaber'' article would fail to specifically name any practitioners of Form VI, only mentioning that all Niman duelists involved in the Battle of Geonosis died. A number of characters are theorized to be Niman practitioners, based on statements from other sources. [[Sora Bulq/Legends|Sora Bulq]] was described as a master of every fighting form, though skill in Niman was never explicitly mentioned.<ref name="Bulq in databank">{{DB|character|sorabulq|Bulq, Sora}}</ref>

In the video game ''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords]]'', the Jedi Masters could teach the [[Meetra Surik|Jedi Exile]] the Niman form only if she was a [[Jedi Sentinel/Legends|Jedi Sentinel]] or the Sentinel's corresponding prestige classes, the [[Jedi Watchman/Legends|Jedi Watchman]] or [[Sith assassin/Legends|Sith assassin]].<ref name="TSL" /> Niman, along with the other lightsaber forms, appears in ''[[Star Wars Galaxies]]'' as part of moves and techniques employable by Jedi characters. This has not definitively been clarified to be canonical.<ref name="SonyCite-Jedi Abilities: Learning the Way">{{SonyCite|url=en_US/players/content.vm?id=66843&resource=features|text=Jedi Abilities: Learning the Way}}</ref>
